title: I Forwarded the Family Chat to the Person They Were Planning Around

parts.text: I was holding the receipt that proved my sister had been lying about the guest list for four years. It was a Costco cake receipt, Saturday, vanilla with a sheet of edible flowers, name: LEAH - DO NOT TELL MAYA. I am Maya. I am thirty-one if you count the way family counts, which is poorly. We were in a suburban Costco parking lot because my mother wanted bulk napkins for a "small dinner." My sister, Leah, had said it was just cousins. The receipt was in the cart under a rotisserie chicken that smelled like rosemary and plastic. I photographed it. Leah came back with soda. "What are you doing?" I held up the paper. She laughed the little laugh. "It's a surprise for you, dummy." The date was last Saturday. I had been at work. I opened the family group chat on my other phone, the one they think I don't use because I left the original chat after a fight. "That's private." I said, "My name is in the title." Mom appeared with napkins. "Don't make a scene in Costco." The automatic doors kept opening for a guy with a flat of water. "Four years?" Her face said yes before her mouth could invent no. Then my actual phone rang. It was my cousin Priya, who is on the real guest list, asking what time to arrive to the dinner they told me was cancelled.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Priya is calling about a dinner they said was cancelled, and the silent thread is still named Maya Filter.

social.video_title: The cake receipt said do not tell Maya — Part 1/2
social.description: Costco parking lot, rosemary chicken, and a group chat titled Maya Filter. The surprise was four years old. Would you have opened the other phone?

parts.text: I answered Priya on speaker. "They told me it was cancelled," I said. Priya went quiet, then swore. Leah hissed, "Hang up." I did not. I forwarded the thread screenshot to Priya, to Uncle Craig, and to Leah's husband, who I like, which made it worse for her. Mom said, "You're destroying the family over cake." I said, "The cake has my exclusion in icing." We sat in the car with bulk napkins and a chicken cooling on my feet. Nobody ate. That night Priya started a new chat without a filter. Half the cousins moved. Leah sent a long message about how I am hard to celebrate because I notice things. I notice things. I skipped the dinner. I bought myself a grocery-store cake with no edible flowers and ate it with Priya on her balcony. It tasted like too much sugar and correct information. Months later Mom asked me to "be the bigger person" for Thanksgiving. I said I would come if my name was on the guest list in writing. She thought that was a joke. I arrived with a printed list she had to check like a clipboard teacher. Leah rolled her eyes and still hugged me for the photo. I let her. I keep the Costco receipt in a kitchen drawer next to takeout menus. Sometimes I show friends. It did, a little. Then it stopped being a mystery, which is a different kind of hunger, and I don't miss the mystery at all.

social.video_title: I took the Maya Filter chat public — Part 2/2
social.description: Speakerphone in a Costco lot, bulk napkins, and a grocery-store cake on a balcony. I RSVP with a printed list now. Would you have skipped the dinner?
